name: PCF85063A real-time clock breakout
description: NXP PCF85063A real-time clock/calendar: seconds to years in BCD with leap-year handling, alarm, countdown timer, offset calibration, one RAM byte and a programmable CLKOUT square wave (32.768 kHz to 1 Hz), on a 400 kHz I2C bus at address 0x51. Chip runs on 0.9-5.5 V (1.8-5.5 V with I2C active) and draws about 0.22 uA when timekeeping. Sold as: Soldered Electronics Real time clock RTC PCF85063A breakout (SKU 333051; 4-pin header SCL, SDA, VCC, GND plus 3-pin header CLK-OE, CLK-OUT, INT on the opposite edge, two easyC/Qwiic connectors, 3.3 V regulator, I2C level shifter with 10 kOhm pull-ups, CR2032 holder), I2C address 0x51.
eli5: A tiny clock that keeps the date and time, even while your board is switched off if a coin cell is fitted.

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock, up to 400 kHz. 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC on the board (JP1), level-shifted to the chip

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data. 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC on the board (JP1), level-shifted to the chip

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply 3.3-5 V into the on-board 3.3 V regulator; also the I2C pull-up rail, so use 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico

pins.name: CLK-OE
pins.description: CLKOUT enable input, pulled HIGH (enabled) by 10 kOhm on the board; drive LOW to switch CLKOUT off. Not needed for basic use

pins.name: CLK-OUT
pins.description: Square-wave output, push-pull, 32.768 kHz at power-on (3.3 V logic). Not needed for basic use

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Alarm/timer interrupt, open-drain, active LOW, 10 kOhm pull-up to 3.3 V on the board. Not needed for basic use

buildNotes: Fixed I2C address 0x51 (A2h write / A3h read); only one PCF85063A per bus.
The two headers sit on opposite edges (SCL/SDA/VCC/GND on one, CLK-OE/CLK-OUT/INT on the other), so wire the board with jumper leads rather than plugging it into the breadboard.
The SCL/SDA header pins are pulled up to VCC with 10 kOhm (jumper JP1): power VCC from 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico so the bus never sees 5 V.
Read or write all seven time registers (04h-0Ah) in one burst, finished within 1 s; the chip blocks its counters during the access.
Bit 7 of the seconds register (OS) is set at first power-up or after the oscillator stopped: the time is invalid until you set it. Setting the time clears it.
Set STOP (Control_1 bit 5) while writing the time and clear it afterwards; keep CAP_SEL = 0 (7 pF), which matches the board's crystal.
CLKOUT runs at 32.768 kHz from power-up; write COF = 111 (Control_2 bits 2-0) or pull CLK-OE low to switch it off.
If the board was not powered up from 0 V, send the software reset (58h to register 00h) to load the reset values.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from pcf85063a import PCF85063A

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
rtc = PCF85063A(i2c)
rtc.datetime((2027, 2, 28, 23, 59, 57))  # Sunday 28 Feb 2027 (not a leap year), 23:59:57
while True:
    y, mo, d, wd, h, mi, s = rtc.datetime()
    print('wd=%d %04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d' % (wd, y, mo, d, h, mi, s))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Keeps the time it was set to and rolls from 28 Feb into 1 March 2027

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (7 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
